title: Part
spec: Create a new coordinate system with Euler angles set to zero and a translation vector of 0.0, 0.0, 0.7463. For the first face, start by drawing an arc that begins at coordinates (0.0, 0.004), passes through (0.0021, 0.001), and ends at (0.0057, 0.0). Follow this with a vertical line from (0.0057, 0.0) to (0.0057, 0.004), and then a horizontal line from (0.0057, 0.004) back to (0.0, 0.004). For the second face, draw another arc starting at (0.0057, 0.0), passing through (0.0087, 0.0013), and ending at (0.0104, 0.004). Complete this loop with a horizontal line from (0.0104, 0.004) to (0.0057, 0.004) and a vertical line from (0.0057, 0.004) down to (0.0057, 0.0). Scale the entire two-dimensional sketch by a factor of 0.0104. Transform the scaled sketch into three dimensions by rotating it with Euler angles set to zero and translating it using the vector (0.0, 0.0, 0.7463). Finally, extrude the sketch 0.0037 units along the normal direction to create a solid body. The final dimensions of the semi-cylindrical shape with a flat top and bottom are: length of 0.010445827946879776, width of 0.004024434422376308, and height of 0.00373134328358209.

reference.label: Reference (dataset)
reference.code:
import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch for the semi-cylindrical shape
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.004) \
     .threePointArc((0.0021, 0.001), (0.0057, 0.0)) \
     .lineTo(0.0057, 0.004) \
     .lineTo(0.0, 0.004) \
     .close() \
     .moveTo(0.0057, 0.0) \
     .threePointArc((0.0087, 0.0013), (0.0104, 0.004)) \
     .lineTo(0.0057, 0.004) \
     .lineTo(0.0057, 0.0) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch to create the semi-cylindrical shape
r = r.extrude(0.0037)

# Translate the shape to the specified position
r = r.translate((0.0, 0.0, 0.7463))

# Final model
r  # This will represent the final model

import cadquery as cq

# Create a new workplane
r = cq.Workplane("XY")

# Define the sketch
r = r.moveTo(0.0, 0.0) \
     .lineTo(0.0104, 0.0) \
     .threePointArc((0.0052, 0.004), (0.0, 0.0)) \
     .close()

# Extrude the sketch
r = r.extrude(0.0037)

# Apply the coordinate system transformation
# Note: CAD-Query does not directly support Euler angles, but we can use rotate and translate methods
# The given Euler angles (-90, 0, -90) correspond to a rotation of 90 degrees around the X-axis and then 90 degrees around the Z-axis
r = r.rotate((0, 0, 0), (1, 0, 0), 90) \
     .rotate((0, 0, 0), (0, 0, 1), 90)

# Define the initial coordinate system transformation
translation_vector = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0037)
euler_angles = (0.0, 0.0, 0.0)

# Create the sketch
sketch = cq.Workplane("XY").transformed(rotate=euler_angles, offset=translation_vector)

# Define the arcs
arc_1 = sketch.moveTo(0.0, 0.004).threePointArc((0.002, 0.0019), (0.004, 0.0))
arc_2 = arc_1.threePointArc((0.0052, 0.0019), (0.0064, 0.0038))
arc_3 = arc_2.threePointArc((0.0052, 0.0037), (0.004, 0.0037))
arc_4 = arc_3.threePointArc((0.002, 0.0019), (0.0, 0.004))

# Close the sketch
sketch = arc_4.close()

# Extrude the sketch

r = sketch.extrude(extrusion_depth)

import cadquery as cq

# The part is a half-elliptical cylinder:
# - Cross-section: half ellipse with X semi-axis 0.0052 (width 0.0104)
#   and Y semi-axis 0.0040 (flat edge at max Y, curved part toward min Y)
# - Extruded along Z by 0.0037

rx = 0.0104 / 2.0   # semi-axis along X
ry = 0.0040         # semi-axis along Y
h = 0.0037          # height along Z

r = (
    cq.Workplane("XY")
    .moveTo(-rx, 0)
    .lineTo(rx, 0)
    .threePointArc((0, -ry), (-rx, 0))
    .close()
    .extrude(h)
)
